newsitem.title: USA: Lilly settles litigation, sees Q2 costs.
newsitem.headline: Lilly settles litigation, sees Q2 costs.

text.p: Eli Lilly and Co said Monday it has reached a settlement with a number of retail pharmacy and supermarket chains relating to certain alleged pricing practices which will trim the pharmaceutical company's 1997 second quarter earnings by $0.02 to $0.03 a share.

The settlement resolves a significant portion of remaining litigation in which Lilly and numerous other U.S. prescription pharmaceutical companies were alleged to have engaged in a pricing conspiracy and price discrimination in violation of the Robinson-Patman Act, Lilly said in a news release.
The Robinson-Patman Act prohibits price discrimination.

The lawsuits were gathered into a class action, which was settled in mid-1996. The cases covered by the settlement announced Monday were among those whose litigants opted out of the class settlement, Lilly said.
A handful of cases remain unsettled, the company said.
"This action will result in a one-time expense that will be recognized in the 1997 second-quarter results and will reduce earnings per share by $.02 to $.03 in the quarter," Lilly said.
Specific terms of the settlement were not disclosed.
